questions.q: What do people with a growth mindset believe about their abilities?
a: They can grow them through hard work and practice
They are set at birth and rarely change
They depend mostly on natural talent
They improve only with the right teacher
questions.why: The overview contrasts this with the fixed mindset, which treats talent as everything.

questions.q: What does the summary say corporate culture pushes employees to do?
a: Focus on looking talented rather than performing well
Take more risks to impress their managers
Ask for training whenever they struggle
Compete openly over who learns fastest
questions.why: Lesson 1 says workers spend their time trying not to look stupid instead of working productively.

questions.q: How do children with a growth mindset react to hard math problems?
a: They want more problems of the same kind
They avoid them until they feel ready
They ask for easier work instead
They worry about their grades
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the children enjoy the satisfaction of pushing themselves, not just better grades.

questions.q: How did Lou Gerstner's approach at IBM differ from Lee Iacocca's at Chrysler?
a: He leveled hierarchies and learned from past failures
He took all the credit for the turnaround
He surrounded himself with loyal admirers
He fired designers who challenged his image
questions.why: Lesson 2 sets Gerstner's teamwork and learning against Iacocca's need for approval.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest saying to yourself after spilling coffee?
a: That it was a one-time accident you can clean up
That you are a clumsy person by nature
That the cup was badly designed
That you should stop drinking coffee
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to treat the failure as external and temporary rather than part of your identity.
